Subject: LedgerLytics — post-call recap & request: sample prompts and model recommendations

Thanks again for the call earlier, Samir — good conversation and appreciation for the detail you shared about the customer support workflows and high-priority edge cases. Quick recap and the asks we discussed: 

Summary (2 min):
- Primary goal: reduce time-to-first-resolution on support tickets via an LLM assistant that drafts responses and surfaces relevant KB articles.
- Typical prompt surface: short user messages (1–3 sentences) plus ticket metadata (category, previous replies).
- Safety/PII: some tickets include names, account numbers, and occasional credit-card fragments 

What Redwood recommends next (concrete):
1) Sample prompt set (ask): 50–100 real user messages (no attachments) — include the ticket text and the intended outcome (reply suggested, escalate, request docs). Redaction guidance below.
2) Benchmark: we’ll run a model-fit benchmark across two size tiers and share results (latency / cost / quality) and a small eval set (10 golden examples).
3) Timeline: if you can share samples by EOD Wed (14 Jul), we’ll have a first-pass evaluation by Fri.

Model recommendations (initial):
- Baseline: smaller LLM (lower cost) for short summarization and draft replies; we’ll test quantized variants.
- Quality tier: medium GPT-style open weights (higher-quality completions) for escalations and tone-sensitive replies.
- Fallbacks: predictably route time-sensitive requests to the faster model; use higher-quality model for agent-facing drafts.

Redaction guidance (please anonymize before sending):
- Replace full names with <REDACTED_NAME>.
- Replace account IDs with <REDACTED_ACC>. Keep zip codes or region tags if they’re important to the intent.
- Remove full credit card numbers (replace last 4 with XXXX).
- If a ticket references an attached file, include a short description rather than the file content.

Attached: prompt_collection_template.csv — simple two-column CSV (raw_ticket_text, desired_outcome) to make ingestion straightforward.

Next steps:
- If you’re comfortable, drop the CSV (anonymized) back to this thread. Priyom (CC) will prepare the benchmark and an initial model recommendation doc. Ben will follow up on procurement/contract questions.

Thanks — talk soon,
Evelyn

On Wed, Jul 14, 2027 at 09:18 AM Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@ledgerlytics.com> wrote:
> Thanks, Evelyn — good summary. A few quick notes from our side: 
> 
> 1) We can produce a 75-example set by Thursday afternoon (14 Jul) — will run the redaction rules you provided. I’ll include two buckets: 'agent-drafts' and 'auto-suggest'.
> 2) On redaction: we need clarity on whether you prefer that we replace customer names with placeholders OR hash them (we have an internal de-id pipeline). Hashing preserves uniqueness across tickets but still counts as a derivative identifier. Any preference from your eval process?

Good questions — quick answers below: 
- Hashing vs placeholders: For the initial model-fit benchmark we prefer placeholders (e.g., <REDACTED_NAME>) since hashing introduces tokens that may bias retrieval/similarity features; placeholders are easier for the eval scripts. If you need to preserve referential uniqueness across examples (e.g., same customer in multiple tickets), share an auxiliary mapping file with hashed IDs but keep the primary CSV with placeholders.
- Data retention & storage: Redwood’s evaluation pipeline stores the anonymized CSV in a short-lived S3 bucket (30 days) scoped to the benchmark job. We do not surface raw unredacted content in logs. We’ll provide a link to the bucket and a deletion ticket when the job completes.
- Model recommendations (quick):
   * Candidate A (cost-efficient): quantized 7B variant — good for quick drafts and high throughput. Expect median latency ~60–80ms for 128-token responses on our Dedicated hardware.
   * Candidate B (quality tier): 13–16B dense variant — better on style, escalation detection and nuanced agent-tone. Latency ~120–180ms but significantly higher ROUGE/semantic-match on our sample tests.

I’ve attached a short redaction_examples file with before/after rows to show how we prefer placeholders. Also linking our benchmark playbook and a lightweight eval script (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cBenchmarkingPlaybook

I’ll ingest your CSV when you confirm the final anonymization format. Priyom
